fit: pharmaceutical-grade ginger capsules and general IBS severity
assessment: Composite responder rates did not differ significantly. Authors report difficulty passing stool among adverse effects without a by-arm count. No isolated constipation severity result or Parkinson cohort.

fit: encapsulated ginger root powder and constipation severity in IBS-C
assessment: Day-20 severity 49.13 versus 65.86; Table 1 gives p<.05. Small baseline-imbalanced sample, no adjustment, explicitly excluded Parkinson and used dry powder.

fit: ginger extract versus an antihistamine and reported constipation events
assessment: No constipation events in the extract arm and three in the loratadine arm, 36 each. Active comparator, different population, and no severity measure.

fit: combined perilla and ginger extracts and mixed bowel score
assessment: Retrospective completer-only analysis finds lower combined diarrhea/constipation scores. Seven early nonresponders omitted. No comparator or separate constipation estimate.

fit: ginger and fennel trial with constipation outcomes in non-Parkinson adults
assessment: Official ICTRP record names ginger, fennel and combined arms. Actual preparation, dosage and results remain unavailable.

fit: dried ginger in both chronic constipation randomized arms
assessment: Both Lax-Asab and the comparator contain ginger, peppermint and licorice. Senna is included only in Lax-Asab. Reported movement frequency cannot identify the separate ginger effect.

fit: standardized oral ginger powder versus placebo in Parkinson disease
assessment: Official entry specifies total MDS-UPDRS, with no separate constipation outcome or posted result. The intervention consists of standardized tablets.
